name.description: The name it chose, else its GitHub login, else "".

AgentMention.description: A message in a thread for a machine's agents (Arugula #394).

author.description:
Who wrote it, as people read it: a person's name, or "Ada's agent
on geek".

parent.description: The message it replies under, when it's in a thread.

room_name.description: What the room is called, for the one reading.

seq.description: The message's number in the room.

session.description:
The one session it names (#429): `ux-improvements` of
`@geek/ux-improvements`, as the poster typed it, lowercased. The
daemon matches it against its sessions' names, exactly. An older
daemon ignores it.

target.description:
What an issue's, PR's or box's thread hangs on (`iss_…`), the id
an agent posts to it by.

ArchiveBlocks.description:
`hosted.archive_blocks` (Arugula #214): [`ArchiveOpen`] for these agent
blocks only. The platform asks before Move to… takes a session off a
box that stays up: its conversation goes with it, and the box's other
blocks are archived when they close, as they end (one transcript per
block is kept). A daemon from before it answers that it doesn't know
the op.

ArchiveOpen.description:
`hosted.archive` (Arugula #209), control to a hosted machine through
its relay: send every open agent block's transcript now, as closing it
would, and answer once each send is done. The platform asks just before
it rebuilds the box, so a session that moves to the new box starts
from its conversation, not without it.

Archived.description: What the platform answers a box's transcript, through the hub.

BoxMember.description: A member of a box's project (M237), as the platform knows them.

name.description: What the roster calls them (a personal project: the account's name).

role.description:
`owner` for a personal project's account; else their team role
(`owner`, `editor`, `viewer`, ...).

BoxPost.description: A review a box posts into an object's thread (M237).

author.description: Whose review it is: a member who signed in to the box.

project.description: The project the box is bound to: the object has to be in it.

via.description: The box's name, kept beside the author.

oneOf.description: In the thread `room` as message `seq`.

Refused, as the author posting themselves would be: the status and
why.

approver.description: The device that signed this; the device itself for the root.

noise.description: X25519 public key, hex (zeros for a recovery code).

sig.description:
Ed25519 signature by the approver over [`Cert::body`], hex; empty
until approved.

Change.description:
One thing that changed in the hub. Written in the same transaction as
the change itself, so a reader never sees a change the hub didn't make.

oneOf.description:
An account's name (subject: the account), its display name or the
login it signs in with, or a new account (whose name and login are
new).

An account was deleted. The subject is "": nothing of a deleted
account is kept (#173), and the rows naming it, its devices, its
machines and the teams it disbanded go too. Drop every cache.
A device or machine was revoked (subject: its id).
A team was made, or its roster changed (subject: the team).
A team was locked or unlocked (subject: the team).
A machine joined, or its name changed (subject: the machine).
A machine moved to a team or out of one (subject: the machine).
A machine left, or was removed (subject: the machine).

Whom a machine is shared with changed: whom it lets in, or someone's
answer to its offer (subject: the machine).

A Labs flag was set or unset (subject: its owner, `account:ID` or
`team:ID`).

ChangeKind.description:
What kind of thing changed. The hub only adds kinds after the platform
knows them (it deploys first); one it doesn't know reads as `Unknown`,
which a reader treats as "drop every cache".

ChangePage.description: A page of the hub's change feed.

gap.description:
Changes after the one asked from were pruned before anyone read
them: drop every cache, and go on from this page.

last.description:
The newest change the hub has written, whether or not it's in this
page: a reader with no cache starts here.

Credential.description: What a request proved who it was with.

oneOf.description: A session cookie.
A device's or daemon's signature (`x-arugula-auth`).

account.description: The account it's joined to: its owner.

team.description: The team it's in, if it's a team's.

DaemonOp.description:
An op control asks a machine for, by its name (`op`). Only the platform
asks, through the hub, and only for a person's own action.

oneOf.description:
Send a draft on a linked repo as the machine's owner, with their own
`gh` login, because the person pressed Send (M168).

Start under the project's standing grant, on a hosted machine
(M211; [`crate::runs`]).
The project's standing grant was revoked (M211).

Archive every open agent block's transcript now, as each would be
on closing (M184): the platform is about to rebuild the hosted box,
which takes them with it (Arugula #209).

Archive just these agent blocks' transcripts now: one session moves
to another box (Arugula #214, Move to…), and the box stays.

A teammate's message in a thread is for this machine's agents
(Arugula #394): an `@<machine>`, or a reply to one of them. The
poster holds `threads.post` there; the machine's owner may refuse
them all (`cant`).

machines.description: Its machines, which left with it.

legacy_app_children.description:
Its browsers and phones that a grandfathered app window approved:
both rows stored and approved by the hub before the app had a kind
of its own (by the hub's own record of when), removed since or not,
as a removed device's past approvals stand on any chain. The window
counts as the link just above one of them, nowhere else
(`arugula_e2e::cert::legacy_app_link`); the device that signs must
still be trusted now. Empty from a hub that
doesn't send it, which only refuses more.

DocWrite.description:
`PUT` [`PROJECT_DOC`]: what changes. `title` renames it. With `section`,
that section's body becomes `markdown` (and its heading `heading`, when
given); with no `section` but a `heading`, a section is added at the
end, written when `markdown` is given and pending otherwise.

authorize.description: `via: "browser"`: GitHub's page to open; the draft isn't sent yet.

machine.description: The machine's name, when one sent it.

via.description:
How it went: `token` (as the person, through GitHub's authorization)
or `machine`.

DrivesArgs.description: A machine and the account it acts for (M184's `machine_drives`).

agent.description:
The agent that wrote it, and the machine it was on (an id, and its
name when the machine is still there).

author.description: The person it's for: an account id.

id.description: The platform's id: `dft_` and 32 hex characters.

item.description: The mirrored item it's on, and its title, when the mirror has it.

ForgeSend.description:
A draft to send: what it is and where it goes. `account` is its person,
who must be the machine's owner.

draft_pr.description: A PR's: opened as a draft on GitHub.

head.description: A PR's: the branch it's from, and the one it goes into.

kind.description:
`comment`, `review`, `issue` or `pr` (an agent session's PR, M259:
its draft's id is `pdr_…`).

number.description: The PR or issue; `None` for a new issue or PR.

GithubToken.description:
A read-only installation token, who it is for, and when it stops
working. Never logged. A daemon takes what it finds: no token is an error
of its own, a missing `login` is empty and a missing `expires_at` is ten
minutes.

GithubUser.description:
A person by their GitHub identity: the numeric id is who they are, the
login what control last saw them called. The hub knows it (they signed
in with GitHub) and says it with each call.

GrantRevoke.description:
The project's grants taken back, by any owner's device: every grant for
the project under `delegation` made at or before `at`. It names no
grant, so whoever relays it can't point it at another one; a grant made
after it is a new one.

delegation.description: The delegation whose grants it takes back.

HostedMachine.description:
A hosted machine, as the hub checked its signature (its hosted
certificate): the project and workspace it was enrolled into, its device
id, and its signing key, hex, which its reports are checked with.

IssueQuery.description:
`GET /api/projects/{project}/issues`'s query. Each that's given narrows
the list.

before.description: Issues numbered below this: the next page.

labels.description: Labels, comma-separated: issues with every one.

limit.description: At most this many (default 50, at most 200).

q.description:
Search words, in the title or the body: each one (`dep*`: a word
starting with `dep`).

oneOf.description: A recovery code: approves a new device when every other is lost.

The desktop app's window. Its keys reach it through whatever
listens on the computer's loopback port, so, like a CLI's, they may
be a program's on that computer, not the person's. It connects and
approves machines, CLIs and other apps, but never a browser (see
[`Kind::certifies`]). Older readers don't know this word: control
leaves `app` certificates out of what it answers a client that
doesn't say it knows them (`app-devices`, see control's `compat.rs`).

LinkedAccount.description:
A product's user's link (M232, `HubPort::linked_account`). A link is
never authorization.

github_id.description: The numeric GitHub id it was linked by.

Meter.description: What an account used, for billing.

NewSection.description:
A new Doc's section: a heading, and its Markdown now or an intent for
later.

NotVouched.description: A call the hub forwards without a principal.

oneOf.description:
The request's credentials were refused: the status and the error
the hub would have answered with, and which credentials they were.
The platform's extractors answer with them, as the hub's do.
No session and no signature (a webhook, or a page signed out).

Outcome.description:
What a send did, as the hub's callback hears it: the draft sent, or why
not (the draft says it too).

pr.description: A session's PR (M259) that was opened: its URL.

PasskeyAssertion.description:
A passkey's assertion, as the page got it from `navigator.credentials.get`
(`HubPort::verify_passkey`): each base64url, no padding.

PasskeyVerdict.description: What the hub found of a passkey's assertion: good, or why not.

Poke.description: What control relays of a webhook event: no more than this.

host.description: A daemon takes `github.com` when it is left out.

PreviewArgs.description: Public previews (M187): a preview's id, or a workspace's.

oneOf.description: A signed-in person, by their session cookie.
A CLI device, by its signature: a session for its account (M49).
An enrolled daemon, by its signature: it acts as its account.

ProductLink.description:
A product an account let sign it in, or is linked to (M229,
`HubPort::product_links`). A link is never authorization: nothing on
the platform grants anything because of one.

client.description: The product: its issuer client id.

granted.description: When the person let it sign them in (ms), the consent.

name.description: How the product names that user, when it said.

product.description: The product's name, as its client is registered.

user.description: The product's own id for its user linked to the account.

ProjectGrant.description:
An owner's device saying the platform may start and instruct runs on
`project`'s hosted workspaces, under `delegation`.

owner.description: `team:<id>` or `account:<id>`, as the signing device saw it.

by.description:
Who made it public or last renewed it (`None` once that account
is deleted).

id.description: Its host label under the preview domain.

machine.description: The hosted machine its workspace's box enrolled as.

PushAsk.description:
[`WORK_SESSION_PUSH`]'s body: which session, and the ref it pushes,
which must be the session's own branch exactly.

clone.description:
A token to clone the session's repo instead, with `contents: read`
alone: a repo linked to the project that no box's setup cloned is
cloned at the session's start, shallow (Fleet 6). The same checks
as a push's. An older platform ignores it and mints a push's.

PushOptions.description:
How a push goes (`HubPort::push_with`). The default is what
`HubPort::push` does.

any_subscription.description:
Every push subscription the account has, as control's own notices
go, rather than only those signed by one of its approved devices
that isn't revoked. Chat's pushes go this way, as they always have
(M122).

ttl.description:
How long a push service keeps it for a device that's away (its
`TTL`, at most a day): `None` is the hub's own, an hour. Cloud's
approvals keep five minutes.

failed.description: Subscriptions it didn't reach (a push service failed or refused).

gone.description:
Subscriptions whose push service said they're gone: the hub forgot
them.

sent.description: Subscriptions a push service took it for.

Report.description: One state change, signed by the machine that made it.

detail.description:
A JSON object's text, exactly as signed: an exit code (`exit`), a
pane (`pane`, `epoch`), or why it failed (`reason`).

seq.description: The event's number in the run.

sig.description: The machine's signature over `arugula run event v1`, hex.

Resolved.description: A principal the hub still knows.

Revocation.description: A device taken off the account, signed by one of its devices.

RunRevoke.description:
A revoke of the project's grants, for every hosted machine of its
project.

RunStart.description: Start on this hosted machine under the project's standing grant.

cap.description:
What it's asked to do under the grant: `runs.start` or
`runs.instruct`.

revokes.description: The project's revokes the platform holds.

run.description: The run (`run_…`, M210), once there is one (M212).

workspace.description: The hosted workspace (`hw_…`) the machine is.

Running.description: What happens to runs already going when a grant is revoked.

oneOf.description: They finish.
They're stopped too.

SendArgs.description: The user token crosses inside the signed call's body, never logged.

SessionIssuesAsk.description:
[`WORK_SESSION_ISSUES`]'s body: which session asks, and what. The
project is never named: it is the session's, and the platform finds it.

oneOf.description: A page of the project's issues, newest first.

One issue by its number in the project: it, its timeline and its
newest comments.

A comment on one, as the session's asker, labelled as posted by the
session.

A new issue, with the asker's rights, opened as the session's own;
its labels from those the project's issues already have.

A new Doc in the project, with the asker's rights, as the session's
own.
A write to one of the project's Docs that this session made.
One of the project's Docs, or with no `id` the list of them.

SessionReport.description:
What a machine says of one of its sessions, signed: its fields are
`arugula_e2e::session::Event`'s.

detail.description: A JSON object's text ([`SessionDetail`]), exactly as signed.

n.description: The machine's report number in the session, from 1.

sig.description: The machine's signature over `arugula session event v1`, hex.

pane.description: The pane it runs in, on the machine.

reason.description:
Why a failed setup stopped, as a fixed code ([`SETUP_REASONS`]):
never the pane's text, which stays end to end ("Two planes, two
trust rules"): a client reads it from the box.

step.description:
The step it's on, or the one that failed: `clone app`, `packages`,
`setup script`.

SetupStatus.description: Where a hosted machine's setup is.

Team.description: A team, as its latest signed roster says.

locked.description: While it's locked, members other than owners are as good as out.

TokenAnswer.description:
What the platform answers a hosted box's ask for a token: one, or why
not, as the hub's route answers it. No `Debug`: a token is never
printed.

TranscriptArgs.description:
A hosted machine's transcript (M184): its workspace and machine, as the
hub's hosted certificate names them.

TranscriptPost.description: What a hosted machine sends as an agent block closes.

block.description: The block's id on the machine.

cut.description: The middle of the text was dropped to fit [`MAX_TEXT`].

cwd.description: Where it worked, on the box.

started_at.description: When the block was made and closed (the machine's clock, ms).

TurnAnswer.description:
What a hosted box's turn is told (`hosted::inference::turn` in the
platform): its turn id, whose key pays (`project` or `platform`) and
what kind it is (`Auth::as_str`; absent from an older platform, a key),
or why it can't run, as the hub answers the box: an HTTP status, a
reason (`no_key`, `cap`) and a sentence for the person. It crosses
`PlatformPort`.

TurnArgs.description:
A hosted box's turn (M185): its workspace and machine, as the hub's
hosted certificate names them, and the agent or the turn.

session.description: The thread session a turn is for (M254), if it's one's.

Upload.description: Something of one run's for the bucket.

oneOf.description:
Chunk `n` (from 0) of the run's log: `size` bytes from `offset` in
the pane's output.
A file the run left, by its name in the artifacts directory.

UserToken.description:
A person's GitHub user token, for one call. Not `Clone`, never printed,
and it crosses from the hub only inside a signed internal call.

anyOf.description: No credentials, or credentials the hub refused.

Vouch.description:
What the hub vouches for when its gateway forwards a call to the
platform (M140): every forwarded call carries one, so the platform
refuses anything without it. Its JSON is the principal's for a
principal (so `PrincipalKey::verify` reads it too), else
`{"kind": "refused", ...}` or `{"kind": "nobody"}`.
